I've got some sensitive info to share with you. APT32 OceanLotus, also known as APT32, is a sophisticated threat actor group linked to Vietnam, and their targeting efforts have been quite... interesting.

From what I've gathered, APT32 OceanLotus has been observed using a combination of spear-phishing attacks, exploit kits, and custom-made malware to compromise high-profile targets in Vietnam, including government officials, military personnel, and journalists.

Their malware of choice, OceanLotus (also known as SeaLotus), is a multi-component malware suite that can deliver a payload to the target's system. It's a bit like a multi-pronged approach, if you will. The malware has been known to exploit vulnerabilities in software, as well as use social engineering tactics to trick users into executing malicious files.

In terms of technical details, OceanLotus has been seen using a combination of HTTP and FTP protocols to communicate with its command and control (C2) servers, often hosted on compromised servers in Vietnam. Their C2 servers are typically located on the following ports: 443 (HTTP), 80 (HTTP), and 21 (FTP). They've also been known to use custom-made SSL/TLS certificates to encrypt their communications,
